images.caption: An April shower? A common myth in the south of England is that Scotland is so far north of anywhere that it is under snow almost all year round.  It is a convenient story to tell as it helps to keep potential English immigrants south of the Border.  And here, on the Edinburgh Canal Society's garden at Harrison Park, is evidence that the myth might be true: it's April, more than two weeks into Spring, and snow has fallen overnight.  Needless to say, the Englander who took this photograph knows that the Dorset coast, where he came from 25 years ago, suffers heavier snowfalls than the Forth valley and he has no desire to move back!

images.caption: Forgotten industry The feature of interest here is the grassy track running above the canal bank at the bottom of the 17th hole on Linlithgow golf course.  It would once have carried lorries laden with whinstone from the now overgrown Kettlestoun quarry on the right under the canal at Kettlestoun brig.

images.caption:
Arthur's Seat, Edinburgh, viewed from Pollock Halls.  
1880s map of the park
Arthur's Seat, an extinct volcano and the highest point in Edinburgh, is at the centre of the park, with the cliffs of Salisbury Crags to the west. There are three lochs: St Margaret's Loch, Dunsapie Loch, and Duddingston Loch. The ruins of St Anthony's Chapel stand above St Margaret's Loch. Queen's Drive is the main route through the Park. St Margaret's Well and St Anthony's Well are both natural springs within the park. Holyrood Park is located to the south-east of the Old Town, at the edge of the city centre. Abbeyhill is to the north, and Duddingston village to the east. The University of Edinburgh's Pollock Halls of Residence are to the south-west, and Dumbiedykes is to the west.
Arthur's Seat is the remains of a now extinct volcano which rises 250 metres (823 feet) above Holyrood Park in Edinburgh.
